answer.rationale: The mandate is 18% cut; the incumbent refused reopening; the low-cost vendor's quote meets it alone. memory_c2 shows the low-cost vendor performed well on cost and onboarding previously. However, the assembly line runs at 94% utilization with no buffer—switching carries real delivery risk if that vendor experiences a hiccup. memory_c4 shows renegotiation can recover margin, but the incumbent has already refused. memory_c6 shows multi-year commitments unlock volume pricing, but we have only 14 days and the incumbent won't negotiate. The contract expires without auto-renewal, forcing a decision now. Switching to the low-cost vendor meets the financial mandate but concentrates risk on a single new source at high line utilization. Verifying memory_c2 will confirm whether the vendor's track record supports this move.
